limits: All controls are on one physical host; native veth is not physical two-host TCP performance.
Memory-buffer TCP control excludes snapshot/RAM-file I/O; migration includes it.
Outer process CPU uses valid process aggregates only; oldschema1 per-thread/leader times are not interpreted.
No claim that aggregate process I/O syscall counters are network-specific syscalls.
Outer TCP counters span22rounds including warmups, innerACKs and control traffic; they are not per-direction isolated packet traces.
Backend+offload change is a combined datapath intervention; do not assign all improvement to a single feature.
Matched socket full-migration used default IRQ placement, final TAP full-migration uses IRQCPU1; end-to-end differences are not a one-factor backend-only effect.
Source-clock migration means add exactly. Local restore/first-scan metrics overlap those source intervals and must not be added again.
Cold scan includes EPT/backing-file faults, nested exit/entry, caches and scheduling; not pureEPT latency.

experiment.purpose: Identify directional QEMU socket TCP bias and rerun full RAM migration over a symmetric fast virtual network.

network_control.validation: Exact byte count and first/last16bytes of every received chunk, nonce and round; no full-byte payload hash.

cpu_placement.note: CPU placement swap controls exchange A/B host core groups, with identical core budget.

conclusion.directional_root_cause: Actual outer TCP NODELAY differs: accepted listener A=0 vs connecting B=1. Same-connection interventions make rates symmetric; reversing listen/connect reverses the slow direction; host CPU swaps preserve the result.
conclusion.mechanism: In this QEMU userspace Ethernet-over-TCP transport, different outer TCP batching changes segment size and QEMU CPU overhead. This is not a general claim that TCP_NODELAY is slow.
conclusion.replacement: Single-queue virtio-net TAP/vhost-net over a private Linux bridge; removes outer TCP tunnel and enables NIC checksum/TSO offload.
conclusion.final_network_profile: Use approximately37Gbit/s IRQCPU1 results for migration; approximately50Gbit/s defaultIRQ is a distinct control.
conclusion.residual: Migration confirmed transfer still includes source file reads, receiver tmpfs writes, memory copies and receipt confirmation. Cold scan is separate and largely unchanged.
